To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Rho kinase is required for the formation of a continuous myelin sheath around an axon by Schwann cells.
ROCK is required for the coordinated wrapping of the Schwann cell membrane around the axonal membrane to form the myelin sheath.
Rho kinase regulates myelination by controlling the organization of actin filaments and myosin light chains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the myelin sheath, the insulating covering of the axons in the peripheral nervous system, is assembled and maintained.
the mechanisms that regulate myelination by Schwann cells and the role of the cytoskeletal proteins in these processes.
the molecular mechanisms of myelination and demyelination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Rho kinase regulates Schwann cell myelination and formation of associated axonal domains.

the mechanisms that control myelin formation are not confined to the node of Ranvier but are distributed along the entire internode.
